ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is a transition-state chemical structure; in the upper part there is a sulfonyl/sulfonamide-like fragment: S is connected to two O by double bonds, and is also connected to one O and one negatively charged N; CO2Me is connected above N. In the lower part there is a carbon skeleton containing O-C-C-D, and two Ph substituents as well as several H labels are shown; there are also curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Then reason: Count by modules and do not count hydrogen-containing bonds such as C-H. The two Ph groups each contribute 6 benzene-ring internal bonds plus 1 C-Ph connecting bond, so this is 2 × (6 + 1) = 14. The sulfonyl/sulfonamide head contributes two S=O, one S-O, and one S-N, totaling 4 bonds. The CO2Me on N contributes N-C, C=O, C-O, and O-Me, totaling 4 bonds. The remaining lower fragment is counted according to the connections in the figure as O-C, C-C, and C-D, totaling 3 bonds; C-H bonds are excluded. The total number is 14 + 4 + 4 + 3 = 25.

raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: First describe the image components, then ignore all curved arrows. Count by modules: two Ph groups contribute 2 × (6 phenyl ring bonds + 1 C-Ph attachment) = 14. The sulfonyl/sulfamate head contributes S=O, S=O, S-O, and S-N = 4 bonds. The CO2Me group on N contributes N-C, C=O, C-O, and O-Me = 4 bonds. The remaining lower fragment contributes O-C, C-C, and C-D = 3 bonds, while C-H bonds are excluded. Sum 14 + 4 + 4 + 3 = 25.
